newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-GRAF BLAMES SHOCK EXIT ON POOR CONFIDENCE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-GRAF BLAMES SHOCK EXIT ON POOR CONFIDENCE.

text.p: Steffi Graf, only a shadow of her once brilliant self when Amanda Coetzer knocked her out of the French Open on Tuesday, said lack of self-confidence was the reason for her shock defeat.

"It was a terrible match," defending champion Graf said after failing to advance to the last four in the Paris tournament for the first time in more than a decade. "I was really nervous starting off the match, feeling very uncomfortable, unsure of my shots."
Graf, who had reached at least the semifinals of the clay event in each of the last 11 years and won five titles along the way, could do very little against a determined Coetzer.
She made a string of unusual unforced errors and hit winners only occasionally to lose 6-1 6-4 after one hour and 32 minutes of a one-sided quarter-final clash.

"I didn't seem to find the reach or the patience at all," said the German second seed after living a nightmare on a miserable afternoon in the French capital. "It's just the state I'm in at the moment. I don't seem to have any self-confidence when I go out there."
South African Coetzer, who had already beaten Graf twice this season, including a 6-0 6-1 annihilation at the German Open in Berlin last month, said she realised that Graf was not at her best,
"She's not playing her best tennis right now," Coetzer, seeded 11th, said. "You can sense that she lacks confidence. She's had some injury problems and maybe she's not 100 percent fit."
Graf, still wearing a bandage on the injured left knee which kept her out of action for three months earlier this year, trailed 6-1 3-1 whe rain interrupted play for some 30 minutes.
After the break she picked up a game a little but missed several opportunities of levelling the second set at 5-5 before going out.
"I was willing to stay out there as long as it was going to take but she was definitely starting to play better," Coetzer said. "It was getting really tight."
But Graf said she had never felt she had a chance of winning the match.

"I sat down during the break but I didn't manage to calm down," said Graf, who lost her temper on several occasions on court, swearing loudly in German. "I just couldn't find the positive attitude I needed."
Graf said she would now take a few days off before preparing for her favourite event, Wimbledon, which she has won seven times.
"I'll probably stop playing tennis for a few days," she said. "That will do me good."
The 27-year old German, who first appeared on the professional circuit 14 years ago, said she had already been through difficult periods in her career.
"It has happened quite a few times," she said. "I think that in anybody's career, you get stages when everything is not quite right. I've been through it already."
Asked why she could not find the confidence she would need to recapture her impressive form of old, she said she just did not know. "I wish I knew but I have no idea," she said.
